skill.name: unreal-engine-developer
skill.description: Expert Unreal Engine 5 developer and technical artist for complete game development via agentic coding. Enables AI-driven control of Unreal Editor through MCP, Python scripting, Blueprints, and C++ for level design, asset management, gameplay programming, and visual development.
skill.summary: Guides AI agents through Unreal Engine 5 editor automation, Python scripting, Blueprint work, and level development.
skill.author: DammianMiller

security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick findings are false positives, but the skill includes real high-risk editor automation. Confirmed risks include screenshot capture, arbitrary Unreal Python and console command execution, all-interface binding guidance, and unpinned third-party MCP server execution. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md or references.md.

remediation.suggestion: Pin MCP package versions or commit hashes, document trusted sources, and require explicit user approval before starting external MCP servers.

remediation.issue: Remote execution may be exposed to the network
remediation.suggestion: Remove the 0.0.0.0 troubleshooting recommendation and prefer 127.0.0.1 with firewall guidance for any deliberate remote access.

remediation.issue: Viewport screenshots can expose project content
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent before screenshot capture, store screenshots locally by default, and document how images may be shared.
Add confirmation guidance before deleting actors, saving levels, importing assets, writing files, or running console commands.

content.user_title: Build Unreal Engine Projects With AI
content.value_statement: Unreal Engine automation often requires switching between editor tools, Python scripts, and Blueprint tasks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through editor control, asset work, level design, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Guides setup for runreal/unreal-mcp and chongdashu/unreal-mcp editor integrations.
Provides Unreal Python patterns for asset creation, import, save, and lookup workflows.
Shows how to spawn, update, duplicate, and delete actors in Unreal levels.
Explains Blueprint class creation, component setup, compilation, and actor spawning.
Includes examples for procedural level generation and batch material assignment.
Defines verification steps for scripts, assets, Blueprints, levels, MCP connections, and screenshots.
limitations: Requires a configured Unreal Engine editor, enabled Python tooling, and a working MCP server.
Setup guidance assumes Unreal Engine 5.4 or 5.5 depending on the MCP option.
Cannot validate project-specific runtime behavior without access to the Unreal project.
Editor automation can modify or delete project assets, so users must review planned changes.

use_cases.title: Prototype Playable Levels
use_cases.description: Create blockouts, place actors, adjust transforms, and verify level changes through Unreal editor automation.

use_cases.title: Automate Asset Pipelines
use_cases.description: Batch import assets, create materials, assign meshes, rename selections, and save updated content packages.

use_cases.title: Build Blueprint Workflows
use_cases.description: Create Blueprint classes, add components, compile assets, and spawn Blueprint actors for gameplay prototypes.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Unreal MCP
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure Unreal Engine for MCP control. Check the required plugins, project settings, and client configuration before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Level
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a small Unreal Engine test level, then create actors, assign meshes, position lights, save the level, and summarize every change.

prompt_templates.title: Clean Up Selected Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my selected Unreal assets, propose a safe batch rename and material assignment plan, then wait for approval before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Blueprint System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Blueprint actor workflow for a reusable gameplay object. Include components, variables, events, validation steps, and rollback guidance.

output_examples.input: Create a small Unreal test scene with a grid of props and simple lighting.
output_examples.output: The skill would provide an editor automation plan, actor placement details, material choices, save steps, and a short verification checklist.

output_examples.input: Prepare selected assets for a technical art review.
output_examples.output: The skill would inspect selected assets, propose naming and material changes, request approval, and describe the final asset updates.

output_examples.input: Create a Blueprint actor for an interactive prototype.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline the Blueprint class, components, variables, event flow, compile checks, and level placement steps.

best_practices: Review every planned editor operation before allowing asset writes, deletes, imports, or console commands.
Keep MCP servers bound to localhost unless a trusted network setup is explicitly required.
Save backups or use source control before running batch Unreal Python or Blueprint automation.
anti_patterns: Running unpinned MCP servers or plugins without reviewing their source and version.
Capturing or sharing viewport screenshots without confirming that project visuals may be exposed.
Using broad Python scripts on production projects before testing them in a disposable level.

faq.question: What does this skill help automate?
faq.answer: It helps AI agents work with Unreal Engine editor setup, Python scripting, asset management, levels, Blueprints, and verification tasks.

faq.question: Does it require an MCP server?
faq.answer: Yes, editor control requires an Unreal MCP setup or another approved path for running Unreal Python commands.

faq.question: Can it modify my project files?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflows include asset writes, level saves, actor changes, imports, and deletes when the connected tools allow them.

faq.question: Can it create Blueprints?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for creating Blueprint classes, adding components, compiling Blueprints, and spawning Blueprint actors.

faq.question: Is screenshot capture required?
faq.answer: No. Screenshots are only useful for visual verification and should require explicit user approval before capture or sharing.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, assuming the user configures compatible MCP access.
